concepts.definition: Overestimating how much others notice one's appearance and actions.
Overestimating how well others can read one's inner states.
Overestimating how common one's own opinions and choices are.

questions.q: What did Gilovich and colleagues (2000) find?
questions.a: People estimated that about twice as many observers noticed an embarrassing T-shirt as actually did.

questions.q: Give a business example of the false consensus effect.
questions.a: A founder who assumes that customers share their preferences and does not test.
